diagnosis: Possible vials, cytopathological preparations, and ancillary techniques for lymph node cytopathology based on ROSE and available laboratory procedures
legend: When FNAB is performed, material can be carefully expelled by air from the reattached syringe (or a stylet as shown here) onto slides for direct air-dried Giemsa-stained or alcohol-fixed Pap-stained smears, or into a liquid-based cytopathology medium or into vials of phosphate-buffered saline (PBS), RPMI medium, buffered normal saline, or formalin, depending on local practice and laboratory requirements. Flow cytometry is the most commonly used ancillary test for lymphoid material placed in PBS, RPMI medium, normal saline, and ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA). Cell blocks can be prepared by various methods from any of these media, as well as from material placed directly into formalin, and they are commonly used for metastatic material. Onsite sample collection should be performed for microbiology tests when an infectious disease is suspected. MGG, May–Grünwald–Giemsa.
